The l-bearing survey variants retain this historical hand-plus-surface compound; bare hath or r-bearing forms require a different or locally justified analysis. The exact regional route may include borrowing between Indo-Aryan languages; the supported family is linked under the user’s preference. RNS uncertainty is source-locality attribution, not lexical reading; tags are retained.

Fruit responses fit directly; groundnut responses may involve specialization or shortening of a modern compound and remain under review. The exact regional route may include borrowing between Indo-Aryan languages; the supported family is linked under the user’s preference.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 2530 eṣa groups the proximal paradigm, with Hindi yah/is, Gujarati e, eastern e/i, and explicit Khowar hes. Survey y/j forms and proximal plurals are paradigm continuations with analogical remodeling; no direct mechanical derivation of each inflected form from nominative eṣa is asserted. The exact regional route may include borrowing between Indo-Aryan languages; the supported family is linked under the user’s preference.
